newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. urges Japan to move on insurance trade issue.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Japan to move on insurance trade issue.

text.p: The United States on Friday urged Japan to resolve a thorny trade dispute over insurance and hinted it could affect Washington's willingness to settle remaining differences over U.S. military bases on Okinawa.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, in talks with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, stressed that "we have to have a relationship where we make progress on both security and economic issues simultaneously and as you know we've made a lot of progress on security issues over the last year," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Christopher told Ikeda the insurance trade issue "has been bedevilling our negotiations (and) something has to be done to move that issue forward. That's a very important issue for the United States. This has to be understood by the Japanese government," Burns told reporters.

On the security side, the spokesman said U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry would visit Tokyo on December 2 for talks and was "hopeful that he might be able to resolve the remaining issues concerning the bases and Okinawa."
"Secretary Christopher urged the Japanese side to make all progress necessary so that Secretary Perry's visit could be successful," Burns said.

He noted how President Bill Clinton's visit to Japan last April reaffirmed U.S.-Japan security ties and stressed "the progress we've made in overcoming the problems that had been caused last year on Okinawa," when the rape of a young girl by U.S. servicemen greatly inflamed local opposition to U.S. military bases there. But in addition to security, Secretary Christopher told Ikeda "it's also very important that we also make progress on ...these very important and sensitive trade issues," Burns said.
